documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI
documents.summary: Short Library & IT guidance on generative AI covering data privacy, output accuracy, bias and copyright. It sets no classroom rule and tells faculty to state their own policies and students to ask.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no ban or permission for coursework; it says 'Faculty should be clear with students ... about their policies on permitted uses, if any', handing class rules to instructors, and otherwise gives data-protection and review advice.

units.why: The preamble 'acknowledges the availability of generative artificial intelligence' tools and says the guidelines 'set forth guidance for the appropriate use'; this is an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56, informs, general.
units.anchor: These guidelines set forth guidance for the appropriate use of generative AI tools at Bucknell.

units.why: Defines generative AI ('a type of artificial intelligence that utilizes deep-learning models') with examples, which sets what the guidelines cover; P61 definition, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI refers to a type of artificial intelligence that utilizes deep-learning models

units.why: States 'No Generative AI tool meets the University's security, privacy, and compliance standards' for anything but public information, a data-protection rule; P50, informs.
units.anchor: No Generative AI tool meets the University’s security, privacy, and compliance standards
units.policy: No generative AI tool meets the University's security, privacy and compliance standards for handling anything besides publicly available information.

units.why: 'You should never enter any institutional data or information protected by ... FERPA into a Generative AI tool' forbids inputting protected data; P50 (protect personal data), must-not since 'never'.
units.anchor: You should never enter any institutional data or information protected by the Family

units.why: Explains that 'Entering data into a Generative AI tool or service is like posting that data on a public website', a rationale about tools storing prompts; P50 informs.
units.anchor: Entering data into a Generative AI tool or service is like posting that data

units.why: Warns that 'Any data you enter ... becomes part of its training data' and could expose sensitive information; a privacy rationale, same type P50 as the preceding units, informs.
units.anchor: Any data you enter into a Generative AI tool becomes part of its training data

units.why: Says output 'can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated (sometimes called hallucinations)', a fact that AI output may be wrong; P31 informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated

units.why: Notes output 'may contain copyrighted material', a copyright concern about AI output; P52, informs. A short clause within the accuracy sentence but a distinct concern.
units.anchor: or may contain copyrighted material

units.why: States AI material 'may exhibit biases and discriminatory ideas or content', naming bias as a harm; P53, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI material may exhibit biases and discriminatory ideas or content.

units.why: 'You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes Generative AI material' makes the user accountable; P29, must.
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish

units.why: 'You should review all outputs from Generative AI for accuracy, including spot-checking of sources or facts, and bias' tells users to verify output; P31, should.
units.anchor: You should review all outputs from Generative AI for accuracy

units.why: 'Faculty should be clear with students ... about their policies on permitted uses, if any' says instructors must communicate their own AI rules and leaves the rule to them; P09 chosen (communicating in class) over P04 since the sentence's action is telling students.
units.anchor: Faculty should be clear with students they are teaching and advising about their policies

units.why: 'Students are also encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies' tells students to ask when unsure; P10, should.
units.anchor: Students are also encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification

units.why: Advises to 'follow security best practices and report suspicious messages' because AI enables phishing and deepfakes; a cybersecurity rule fitting no listed type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Continue to follow security best practices and report suspicious messages
units.uncovered_note: Security awareness: AI-enabled phishing and deepfakes; follow security practices and report suspicious messages to the tech desk.

documents.title: WAC Council Statement on the Use of Generative AI in W Courses
documents.summary: A Writing Program council statement for W courses. W1 courses are urged to ban genAI in the writing process, and W2 courses must include at least one assignment done without genAI. It covers only designated writing courses.
documents.stance_why: For the writing process in W courses it says 'genAI use not be permitted at all in students' writing processes in W1s' and W2 courses 'must include at least one writing assignment ... without any reliance on genAI'; AI is barred in the governed work, with scope limited to W courses, so restrict rather than prohibit.

units.why: The Council 'finds the use of generative AI as part of students' writing processes in W courses to be incompatible with the Program's aims', the reason given for limiting AI; P41 (AI undermines the practice that builds writing skill), informs.
units.anchor: finds the use of generative AI (genAI) as part of students’ writing processes

units.why: Gives the rationale that writing is 'a tool for thinking and learning' and 'a process that enables clarifying, refining, and communicating knowledge'; explains why writing practice matters, P41 informs.
units.anchor: writing as a tool for thinking and learning

units.why: Cites the AWAC statement that situates writing 'as a human-centered activity' as support for the recommendation, an external framework basis; P56 informs.
units.anchor: which situates writing as a human-centered activity

units.why: 'The WAC Council expects that all W courses will ... assign writing to be completed without genAI use' is a default no-AI expectation for writing assignments in W courses; P01, instructor-facing, 'expects' so should.
units.anchor: all W courses will emphasize and assign writing to be completed without genAI use

units.why: 'We recommend that genAI use not be permitted at all in students' writing processes in W1s' bans AI for W1 writing; P01 (default prohibition), should because it is a recommendation.
units.anchor: genAI use not be permitted at all in students’ writing processes in W1s.

units.why: 'W2 courses must include at least one writing assignment ... without any reliance on genAI' requires an assignment design with no AI; P35 (assignment redesign) rather than P01, since the AI-free rule applies to one assignment, not the course default.
units.anchor: must include at least one writing assignment or project that requires students

units.why: Says brainstorming, organizing and editing 'should not be outsourced to genAI', so AI must not replace these thinking steps; P32 (student remains primary thinker) chosen over P15, which covers permitted brainstorming.
units.anchor: they should not be outsourced to genAI.

units.why: Says brainstorming, organizing and editing 'may be supported through classroom activities and individual conversations', pointing to human support in place of AI; P35, may.
units.anchor: may be supported through classroom activities and individual conversations

documents.title: CSCI Common Course Policies (Use of AI section)
documents.summary: The Computer Science department's common course policy section on AI encourages AI for learning, debugging and concepts, if students attribute it (including prompts), submit their own work and verify output. AI drafts of written work need revision, and improper reliance counts as an integrity violation.
documents.stance_why: It opens 'The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning and understanding' and the later guidelines add conditions (attribution, own work), so the stance is encourage rather than a neutral permit.

units.why: 'The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning and understanding' sets a default of encouraged use; P02, encourage.
units.anchor: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning

units.why: 'students must use these tools ethically and responsibly' is a general conduct duty with no specific rule; closest is P29 (responsibility), since the next lines tie it to personal effort, must.
units.anchor: students must use these tools ethically and responsibly.

units.why: 'AI can be a powerful aid in coding, debugging, and conceptual understanding' names permitted uses; P13 chosen as the most specific, may.
units.anchor: AI can be a powerful aid in coding, debugging, and conceptual understanding

units.why: 'it should not be a substitute for personal effort and academic integrity' says AI must not replace the student's own work; P32, should-not.
units.anchor: it should not be a substitute for personal effort and academic integrity.

units.why: 'Any work submitted must be the student's own' requires submitted work to be the student's own; P29, must.
units.anchor: Any work submitted must be the student’s own.

units.why: 'all submitted work should reflect individual effort' adds effort to the ownership idea; P32 chosen over P29 since it stresses the student's own effort when AI assists, should.
units.anchor: all submitted work should reflect individual effort.
units.frag_start: While AI can assist in learning

units.why: 'Plagiarism or reliance on AI to complete assignments without proper understanding will not be tolerated and may result in disciplinary action' classes improper AI reliance as misconduct; P36, must-not, not P37 since no concrete penalty is named.
units.anchor: reliance on AI to complete assignments without proper understanding will not be tolerated

units.why: 'When AI tools are used, proper attribution must be given' requires disclosure of AI use; P24, must.
units.anchor: When AI tools are used, proper attribution must be given.

units.why: Says specific code snippets, solutions, or significant assistance 'should be clearly noted in the submission, including the prompts used', which puts the prompt in the citation; P25 over P24 because of the prompt requirement, should.
units.anchor: this should be clearly noted in the submission, including the prompts used.

units.why: 'AI can be a valuable tool for exploring new concepts' permits AI for learning concepts; P12 (tutor for understanding), may.
units.anchor: AI can be a valuable tool for exploring new concepts

units.why: 'generating ideas' is listed as a valuable use of AI; P15 (brainstorming), may.
units.anchor: generating ideas, and improving coding skills

units.why: 'Students are encouraged to use AI to experiment and learn' repeats the encouragement as an explicit recommendation for hands-on learning; P02, encourage.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use AI to experiment and learn

units.why: 'they should also strive to understand the underlying principles and logic behind the AI-generated content' asks for understanding of AI output; P30, should.
units.anchor: strive to understand the underlying principles and logic behind the AI-generated content

units.why: 'AI tools have limitations and may not always provide accurate or optimal solutions' warns that output can be wrong; P31 informs.
units.anchor: AI tools have limitations and may not always provide accurate or optimal solutions.

units.why: 'Critical thinking and independent verification of AI-generated content are essential' requires students to verify output; P31, should.
units.anchor: independent verification of AI-generated content are essential

units.why: 'AI tools may be used to create drafts and revise written work' permits AI in prose writing; P18 (prose separately), may.
units.anchor: AI tools may be used to create drafts and revise written work.

units.why: 'AI-generated text should not be used verbatim' limits prose use; P18, should-not.
units.anchor: AI-generated text should not be used verbatim.

units.why: 'Students must critically review, edit, and revise any AI-generated content' requires review of AI text; P18 chosen since it is specific to written work (P31 also touches verification), must.
units.anchor: Students must critically review, edit, and revise any AI-generated content

units.why: 'Using AI-generated text without proper revision or personal contribution is unacceptable and will be considered a violation of academic integrity' classes the misuse as misconduct; P36, must-not.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: 'The final submission should reflect the student's own understanding and effort' ties the final work to the student's own understanding; P29, should.
units.anchor: The final submission should reflect the student’s own understanding and effort.
